thesis: Nikola Jokic became the ninth player in NBA history to win three MVP awards in four seasons (2020-21, 2021-22, 2023-24), joining an elite legacy while achieving unprecedented statistical dominance as a center.

facts.claim: Jokic won three MVP awards in four seasons: 2020-21, 2021-22, and 2023-24, finishing runner-up to Joel Embiid in 2022-23.

Only eight other players in NBA history have won three or more MVP awards: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Michael Jordan, Bill Russell, LeBron James, Wilt Chamberlain, Larry Bird, Magic Johnson, and Moses Malone.
Jokic became the first center in six decades to win three MVPs in four seasons, following Kareem Abdul-Jabbar who achieved this from 1973-74 to 1976-77.
In 2023-24, Jokic finished top five in total points, rebounds, and assists, becoming the first player since Wilt Chamberlain in the 1960s to accomplish this.
Jokic is the only player in NBA history to rank top ten in points, rebounds, assists, and steals simultaneously since 1973-74 when the league began tracking steals.
Jokic led the league in Box Plus/Minus for 2023-24 and has led in Player Efficiency Rating for four consecutive seasons, becoming the all-time PER leader ahead of Michael Jordan and LeBron James.

verified_numbers.context: Denver's net rating with vs. without Jokic (largest for any player with 1,000+ minutes in 2023-24)

timeline.event: Jokic wins his first NBA MVP award, becoming a breakout star on the Denver Nuggets.
Jokic wins his second consecutive MVP award and leads Denver to NBA championship.
Joel Embiid wins MVP; Jokic finishes runner-up but Denver wins championship tournament games.
Jokic wins third MVP in four seasons, becoming ninth player in NBA history with three or more MVPs.

topic: Nikola Jokic's unprecedented three-time MVP achievement and historical dominance
